title.narrative: Somalia productive, resilient, and inclusive growth (SPRING) project

description.narrative: Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) Project for Somalia has development objectives to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance. Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector supports legal, regulatory, and institutional reforms and service delivery modernization. Sub-components include Sub-component 1.1: Strengthening institutional and regulatory framework for the private sector, which updates and enacts business-enabling laws and regulations, streamlines and harmonizes the online Somalia Business Registration System (SBRS) across federal, state, regional, and municipal levels, advances effective public–private cooperation, and aligns business regulation with trade integration efforts in regional and global markets, including the East African Community (EAC). Sub-component 1.2: Enhancing the Somali ID System builds the foundational digital identification system by registering five million people, with targeted outreach to women and vulnerable groups; upgrades identity management and security; integrates digital ID verification with high-impact services (such as telecommunications, banking electronic Know Your Customer, passport, and social protection); and strengthens the National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) through policy, capacity, and stakeholder engagement. Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity consolidates financial stability, integrity, and infrastructure. Sub-components include Sub-component 2.1: Operational and capacity-building support to Gargaara, Somalia's apex micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) financing facility, to complete core institutional functions, enhance appraisal and monitoring of participating financial institutions (PFIs), and deliver non-lending support to banks and microfinance institutions (MFIs). Sub-component 2.2: Strengthening financial sector stability, integrity, and infrastructure supports the Central Bank of Somalia (CBS) to issue and implement financial sector laws, depositor and consumer protection frameworks, supervision and macroprudential policies, financial inclusion and climate finance frameworks, and to operationalize the national payments infrastructure including the Somalia Instant Payment System (SIPS) and payment switch; strengthens the Financial Reporting Center (FRC) for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism oversight; and enhances capacity and financial market infrastructure at the Bank of Somaliland (BoS). Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs expands financing and builds firm capabilities. Sub-components include Sub-component 3.1: Derisking access to finance for MSMEs through a scaled risk-sharing mechanism (RSM) that mobilizes private capital to priority productive and climate-vulnerable sectors—such as agriculture, livestock, and fisheries—offers higher coverage for women-owned or managed businesses, aligns fees with Islamic banking practices, and provides operational support and market research. Sub-component 3.2: Enhancing MSMEs resilience delivers tailored business development services (BDS) to improve efficiency, market access, and climate adaptation, with modalities such as voucher-based delivery and measures to facilitate women's participation. Component 4: Project Management establishes a Project Implementation Unit in the Ministry of Finance to coordinate activities, fiduciary and environmental and social framework compliance, monitoring and evaluation, grievance redress mechanisms, gender-sensitive implementation, and cross-government coordination through a Project Steering Committee including core institutions.
